To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
collagenase‐3 is transcriptionally activated by transforming growth factor (Tgf)‐β1 in MDA‐Mb231 cells.
TGF‐beta stimulates collagenase-3 expression in Mda-MB-231 cells through the MAPK and Smads pathways.
TGF‐beta‐1, a crucial metastasis‐promoting molecule, stimulates expression of the collagenase‐3 gene in human breast cancer, and that the MAPK and Smads are involved in this process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism by which TGF‐β stimulates collagenase‐expression.
the molecular mechanism of TGF‐β‐induced collagenase‐3 gene expression in human breast cancer.
the mechanisms of TGF‐β‐mediated collagenase‐3 gene expression and its role in breast cancer bone metastasis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
both MAPK and Smads are involved in Tgf‐β1‐regulated gene expression.
the Smad pathway is essential for TGF‐β‐stimulated collagen‐3 expression in human breast cancer cell lines, whereas the MAPK pathway is not.
the TGF‐beta‐stimulated collagen‐3 expression in human breast cancer MDA-MB231 cells is mediated via both MAPK and Smads signaling pathways.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
collagenase‐3 is a target for TGF‐β in breast cancer and that the TGF‐beta‐induced collagenase‐3 gene expression in breast cancer cells is regulated by the Smad and MAPK signaling pathways.
TGF‐beta1 induces collagenase-3 expression in breast cancer cells via MAPK and/or Smad signaling pathways.
the TGF‐ β1‐induced collagenase‐3 gene expression in MDA ‐ MB231 cells is mediated through both Smads and MAP kinases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TGF‐beta‐1 induces collagenase‐3 in breast cancer cells through both MAPK and Smads pathways.
TGF‐ β1 stimulates collagenase‐ 3 expression in human breast cancer MDA‐ MB231 cells through both Smad and MAPK pathways.
